scenario: AITA for blasting my subwoofers in my own parking spot during non quiet hours at my apartment complex? | Posting from a throwaway for whatever reason, just don't want this to blend into my other subs. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. Not sure. Anyways the complex is really cool because a lot of places won't let you work on your car, well I can pay an extra premium every month to get a mechanics spot under shade. It's an extra 2 bills a month but so worth it. When I work on my car I BLAST my system. It helps me think and focus. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

Most leases include clauses about "unreasonable noise" or " disturbances that interfere with other residents' peaceful enjoyment of their homes." Bass that rattles walls and disrupts sleep (especially for a child’s 8:30 bedtime) qualifies as *unreasonable*, even during daytime hours. - Multiple complaints from neighbors and management confirm this isn’t just one person being sensitive—it’s a pattern of disturbance. 2. **" mechanics spot" doesn’t grant unlimited noise rights**: - Paying extra for a dedicated workspace doesn’t override basic courtesy. This is confrontational and intentionally hostile behavior. - Telling management "I’m not breaking rules" ignores the *spirit* of community living. A good neighbor would proactively adjust their habits when others are genuinely affected, especially when a child’s sleep is involved. 4. **Practical alternatives exist**: - You claim earbuds "just wasn’t the same," but this is a solvable problem. Consider: - Using a *high-quality Bluetooth headset* for music while working (many audiophiles do this). - Installing *soundproofing* in your car (e.g., damping mats) to reduce bass transmission. - Limiting bass-heavy sessions to *earlier* in the day (e.g., before 8:30pm) when fewer people are trying to sleep. - If the system is truly "your life," find a *private* space (e.g., a garage, a soundproofed room) where you can blast it without affecting others. **Final verdict:** You’re not "wrong" for wanting to enjoy your car, but you * are* being inconsiderate by prioritizing your hobby over your neighbors’ right to a peaceful environment. The fact that management has received "complaint after complaint" proves this isn’t a minor issue—it’s a genuine disruption. A responsible tenant would *immediately* adjust their behavior when multiple people report being affected, not argue about "rules" while escalating the problem. **YTA (Yes, you’re the asshole)**. **Action step**: Apologize to your neighbors, use earbuds consistently, and work with management to find a sustainable solution (e.g., soundproofing, limited bass hours). If you refuse to compromise, you risk losing your mechanics spot or facing lease violations. Community living requires mutual respect—not just " following the letter of the law."
